pp:me:2026:q1.question:
Domain $A$ is bounded by curve $x^2 = 4y$ ordinate $x = 2$ and $x$ axis.

The value of $\iint_{A} y \, dx \, dy$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: Domain A is bounded by $x^2 = 4y$ ordinate $x = 2$ and $x$ axis. Step 1: Find limits of integration From $x^2 = 4y \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{x^2}{4}$ For x: 0 to 2 For y: 0 to $\dfrac{x^2}{4}$ Step 2: Set up integral $\iint_A y \, dx \, dy = \int_0^2 \int_0^{x^2/4} y \, dy \, dx$ Step 3: Inner integral $\int_0^{x^2/4} y \, dy = \left[\dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_0^{x^2/4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{x^4}{16} = \dfrac{x^4}{32}$ Step 4: Outer integral $\int_0^2 \dfrac{x^4}{32} \, dx = \dfrac{1}{32} \left[\dfrac{x^5}{5}\right]_0^2 = \dfrac{1}{32} \cdot \dfrac{32}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q2.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:me:2026:q2.question: Let $\varphi$ be a scalar function. Then $\nabla\varphi$ is
options: always perpendicular to the surface of constant $\varphi$
always parallel to the surface of constant $\varphi$
the minimum rate of change of scalar $\varphi$

detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: Gradient of a Scalar Function For a scalar function $\varphi$ the gradient $\nabla\varphi$ is defined as: $\nabla\varphi = \dfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x}\hat{i} + \dfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial y}\hat{j} + \dfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial z}\hat{k}$ Key Properties: (1) $\nabla\varphi$ always points in the direction of maximum rate of increase of $\varphi$. (2) $\nabla\varphi$ is always perpendicular (normal) to the surface of constant $\varphi$ (i.e. the level surface where $\varphi = c$). (3) Its magnitude gives the maximum rate of change (not minimum). (4) It is not always zero. Checking Options: (A) Always perpendicular to surface of constant $\varphi$ -> Correct (B) Always parallel -> Wrong (C) Minimum rate of change -> Wrong (it is maximum) (D) Always zero -> Wrong Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q3.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:me:2026:q3.question:
The order and degree of the following differential equation are $m$ and $n$ respectively.

$\dfrac{\partial^3 \varphi}{\partial x^3} + \dfrac{\partial^2 \varphi}{\partial y^2}\dfrac{\partial \varphi}{\partial x} + \left(\dfrac{\partial^2 \varphi}{\partial x^2}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\partial \varphi}{\partial y} = 0$

The value of $(m - n)$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given PDE: $\dfrac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial x^3} + \dfrac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial y^2}\dfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + \left(\dfrac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x^2}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial y} = 0$ Step 1: Find Order (m) Order = highest order derivative present in the equation. Highest derivative = $\dfrac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial x^3}$ -> Order = 3 So $m = 3$ Step 2: Find Degree (n) Degree = power of the highest order derivative after clearing any fractional powers. The highest order derivative $\dfrac{\partial^3\varphi}{\partial x^3}$ appears with power 1. So $n = 1$ Step 3: Calculate (m - n) $m - n = 3 - 1 = 2$ Note: The term $\left(\dfrac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x^2}\right)^2$ is of order 2 not order 3 so it does not affect the degree of the equation. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q4.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 4
pp:me:2026:q4.question: Newton-Raphson method for solving algebraic equations is based on

detailed_solution.markdown: The Newton-Raphson method is derived from the Taylor series expansion of $f(x)$ about a point $x_n$. Derivation: Expand $f(x)$ using Taylor series around $x_n$: $f(x) = f(x_n) + (x - x_n)f'(x_n) + \dfrac{(x-x_n)^2}{2!}f''(x_n) + \cdots$ Truncating after the first derivative term and setting $f(x) = 0$: $0 = f(x_n) + (x_{n+1} - x_n)f'(x_n)$ Solving for $x_{n+1}$: $x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$ This is the standard Newton-Raphson iteration formula derived from Taylor series. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q5.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 5
pp:me:2026:q5.question:
The exact solution of $\int_0^4 \dfrac{dx}{1+x}$ is represented as $n$.

If $m$ represents numerically evaluated value of the above integral using Trapezoidal rule by considering four equal subintervals in the range of $x$ then $(m - n)$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: $n = \int_0^4 \dfrac{dx}{1+x}$ Step 1: Exact solution (n) $n = \left[\ln(1+x)\right]_0^4 = \ln 5 - \ln 1 = \ln 5 = 1.6094$ Step 2: Trapezoidal Rule with 4 equal subintervals $h = \dfrac{4-0}{4} = 1$ Points: $x_0=0, x_1=1, x_2=2, x_3=3, x_4=4$ $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x}$ $f(0)=1, \; f(1)=0.5, \; f(2)=0.333, \; f(3)=0.25, \; f(4)=0.2$ Trapezoidal formula: $m = \dfrac{h}{2}\left[f(x_0) + 2f(x_1) + 2f(x_2) + 2f(x_3) + f(x_4)\right]$ $m = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 + 2(0.5) + 2(0.333) + 2(0.25) + 0.2\right]$ $m = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 + 1 + 0.667 + 0.5 + 0.2\right]$ $m = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3.367 = 1.6833$ Step 3: $m - n = 1.6833 - 1.6094 = 0.0739 \approx 0.074$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q6.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 6
pp:me:2026:q6.question: A horizontal disk has a radial frictionless slot in which a small block is confined to slide. The disk turns anticlockwise about its centre with a constant angular velocity of 3 rad/s. If the block slides along the slot with a constant speed of 0.2 m/s relative to the slot then the magnitude of Coriolis acceleration in $m/s^2$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Angular velocity $\omega = 3$ rad/s Relative speed of block $\dot{r} = 0.2$ m/s Coriolis Acceleration Formula: $a_{Cor} = 2\omega\dot{r}$ Note: The Coriolis acceleration is given by $2\vec{\omega} \times \vec{v}_{rel}$ where $\vec{v}_{rel}$ is the velocity of the block relative to the rotating frame. Calculation: $a_{Cor} = 2 \times \omega \times \dot{r}$ $a_{Cor} = 2 \times 3 \times 0.2$ $a_{Cor} = 1.2 \, m/s^2$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Machine - Gear and Gear Train
detailed_solution.markdown: An idler gear is a gear that is inserted between the driver and the driven gear to change the direction of rotation. pp:me:2026:q8.question:
In a single degree of freedom vibrating system with only viscous damping the critical damping coefficient is 350 N s/m and the damping coefficient is 35 N s/m.

The logarithmic decrement of the vibrating system is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Critical damping coefficient $c_c = 350$ N s/m Damping coefficient $c = 35$ N s/m Step 1: Damping ratio $\zeta = \dfrac{c}{c_c} = \dfrac{35}{350} = 0.1$ Step 2: Logarithmic Decrement formula $\delta = \dfrac{2\pi\zeta}{\sqrt{1-\zeta^2}}$ Step 3: Substitute values $\delta = \dfrac{2\pi \times 0.1}{\sqrt{1-(0.1)^2}}$ $\delta = \dfrac{0.6283}{\sqrt{1-0.01}}$ $\delta = \dfrac{0.6283}{\sqrt{0.99}}$ $\delta = \dfrac{0.6283}{0.995} = 0.6314 \approx 0.63$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q9.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 9
pp:me:2026:q9.question:
A closely coiled helical compression spring of mean coil diameter $D$ and wire diameter $d$ is loaded by an axial force $F$.

The maximum shear stress developed in the wire is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Mean coil diameter = D Wire diameter = d Axial force = F Two stress components act on the wire cross-section: 1. Direct shear stress due to axial load F: $\tau_d = \dfrac{4F}{\pi d^2}$ Maximum shear stress (without Wahl's correction): $\tau_{max} = \tau_t + \tau_d = \dfrac{8FD}{\pi d^3} + \dfrac{4F}{\pi d^2}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q10.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 10
pp:me:2026:q10.question: The rotor of an aeroplane engine has a mass moment of inertia 1.0 kg $m^2$. The engine rotates at a speed of 500 RPM in the clockwise direction if viewed from the front of the aeroplane. If the aeroplane while flying at 1200 km/hr turns with a radius of 2 km at same elevation then the magnitude of the gyroscopic moment exerted by the rotor on the aeroplane structure in N m is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Mass moment of inertia of rotor $I = 1.0 \, kg \cdot m^2$ Engine speed $N = 500$ RPM Aeroplane speed $V = 1200$ km/hr Turn radius $R = 2$ km = 2000 m Step 1: Angular velocity of rotor $\omega_r = \dfrac{2\pi N}{60} = \dfrac{2\pi \times 500}{60} = \dfrac{1000\pi}{60} = 52.36 \, rad/s$ Step 2: Angular velocity of precession $V = 1200 \, km/hr = \dfrac{1200 \times 1000}{3600} = 333.33 \, m/s$ $\omega_p = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{333.33}{2000} = 0.1667 \, rad/s$ Step 3: Gyroscopic moment $C = I \cdot \omega_r \cdot \omega_p$ $C = 1.0 \times 52.36 \times 0.1667$ $C = 8.73 \, N \cdot m$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q11.question: A rectangular plate is perfectly welded to a gusset plate with parallel fillet weld joints as shown in the figure below. A tensile force $P$ is applied on the plate in a direction parallel to the length of the weld. Assuming the throat of the weld as the weakest section the critical load is

detailed_solution.concept: Machine Design - Bolted, Riveted and Welded Joint
detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Length of weld = $l$ Fillet weld leg size = $h$ Allowable shear strength = $\tau_{all}$ Tensile force = $P$ (parallel to weld length) Two parallel fillet welds (top and bottom) Step 1: Throat thickness of fillet weld For a fillet weld the throat thickness is: $t = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2}} = 0.707h$ Step 2: Throat area for two welds $A_{throat} = 2 \times t \times l = 2 \times \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2}} \times l = \sqrt{2} \, h \, l$ Step 3: Critical load The force P acts as shear on the throat area: $P_{critical} = \tau_{all} \times A_{throat}$ $P_{critical} = \tau_{all} \times \sqrt{2} \, h \, l$ $P_{critical} = \sqrt{2} \, h \, l \, \tau_{all}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q14.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 14
pp:me:2026:q14.question: A steady incompressible laminar flow passes through a $90^\circ$ tube bend placed on a horizontal surface. In horizontal diametric plane two pressure taps $P_i$ and $P_o$ are provided across the cross-section at inner and outer walls of the bend respectively. Which one of the following options is correct?
options: $(P_o - P_i)$ is directly proportional to the bend radius.
$(P_i - P_o)$ is inversely proportional to the average flow velocity.

detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: Flow through a curved path (bend) When fluid flows through a curved path it requires a centripetal force directed towards the centre of curvature. Analysis: In a $90^\circ$ tube bend the fluid follows a curved path. The centripetal acceleration is directed towards the inner wall of the bend. This centripetal force is provided by the pressure difference between outer and inner walls. Pressure equation along radial direction: $\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial r} = \dfrac{\rho V^2}{r}$ where r is the radius of curvature. Since $\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial r} > 0$ pressure increases from inner to outer wall. Therefore: $P_o > P_i$ The outer wall has higher pressure than the inner wall. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q15.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 15
pp:me:2026:q15.question: An ideal gas passes isothermally through a long horizontal uniform cross-section pipe under steady flow. Consider that the pressure gradient in the pipe is sufficient for a finite change in the density of the gas. If the flow of the gas is purely pressure driven and subsonic throughout then the average flow velocity
options: does not change throughout the pipe
increases in the hydrodynamic entrance region and then decreases thereafter

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Isothermal flow of ideal gas through uniform pipe. Pressure gradient causes finite density change. Flow is subsonic throughout. Analysis: For isothermal flow: $T = \text{constant}$ For ideal gas: $P = \rho R T$ Since T is constant: $P \propto \rho$ As gas flows along pipe pressure drops due to friction: $P_1 > P_2 > P_3 \cdots$ Therefore density also decreases along flow: $\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3 \cdots$ Continuity equation for uniform cross-section pipe: $\rho A V = \text{constant}$ Since A is constant: $\rho V = \text{constant}$ As $\rho$ decreases along flow V must increase: $V \propto \dfrac{1}{\rho}$ Therefore average flow velocity increases along the flow. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q16.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 16
pp:me:2026:q16.question: Bernoulli's equation CANNOT be applied between
options: any two arbitrary points in the flow field for steady incompressible rotational flow
any two arbitrary points in the flow field for steady incompressible irrotational flow
any two points along a streamline for steady incompressible flow
any two points along a streamline for steady incompressible rotational flow

detailed_solution.markdown: Bernoulli's Equation applicability: Standard Bernoulli's equation: $\dfrac{P}{\rho g} + \dfrac{V^2}{2g} + z = \text{constant}$ Conditions for applicability: (1) Can be applied between any two points along a streamline for steady incompressible flow (rotational or irrotational). (2) Can be applied between any two arbitrary points (not necessarily on same streamline) ONLY for steady incompressible irrotational flow. Checking each option: (A) Any two arbitrary points for steady incompressible rotational flow -> CANNOT be applied (Correct answer) (B) Any two arbitrary points for steady incompressible irrotational flow -> CAN be applied (C) Any two points along streamline for steady incompressible flow -> CAN be applied (D) Any two points along streamline for steady incompressible rotational flow -> CAN be applied Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q18.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 18
pp:me:2026:q18.question: For the isothermal expansion of an ideal gas in a piston cylinder system the net heat supplied during the process is equal to the net work. Which one of the following statements is correct for the given process?
options: The process is not possible as it violates the second law of thermodynamics.
The process is not possible as it violates the first law of thermodynamics.
The process is possible however it violates the second law of thermodynamics.

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - First Law, Heat, Work and Energy
detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Isothermal expansion of ideal gas in piston cylinder. Net heat supplied = Net work done First Law of Thermodynamics: $Q - W = \Delta U$ For isothermal process of ideal gas: $\Delta U = 0$ (since temperature is constant) Therefore: $Q = W$ This is consistent with the given statement -> First law is satisfied Second Law of Thermodynamics: The process involves an isothermal expansion where heat is completely converted to work. (2) It is a reversible isothermal expansion. (3) The entropy of the universe does not decrease. $\Delta S_{system} = \dfrac{Q}{T} > 0$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2026:q21.title: GATE ME 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 21
pp:me:2026:q21.question: Which one of the following options is NOT an error associated with STereoLithography (STL) file in additive manufacturing?

detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: STL File Errors in Additive Manufacturing STL (STereoLithography) file represents 3D surfaces as a mesh of triangular facets. Common errors associated with STL files: Missing Facet (B): When a triangular facet is absent from the mesh leaving a hole in the surface. This is a valid STL error. Non-manifold topology conditions (C): When edges are shared by more than two facets or geometry is not properly closed. This is a valid STL error. Degenerate facets (D): When a triangular facet has zero area (all three vertices are collinear or coincident). This is a valid STL error. Staircase effect (A): This is NOT an error in the STL file itself. The staircase effect is an artifact that occurs during the slicing and building process in additive manufacturing due to layer-by-layer deposition. It is related to the manufacturing process not the STL file format. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

The table lists the unit selling price of five products P Q R S and T. On a particular day 250 items were sold with the average selling price of Rs. 60.

The following observations were made:
(i) The quantity of S sold was twice that of T.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Product} & P & Q & R & S & T \\ \hline \text{Unit selling price (Rs.)} & 100 & 50 & 40 & 60 & 60 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

What is the quantity of product P sold on that day?

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: Total items sold = 250 Average selling price = Rs. 60 Total revenue = $250 \times 60 = Rs. \, 15000$ Let quantity of T = t Quantity of S = 2t Quantity of R = 3t Quantity of Q = 4t Quantity of P = p Step 1: Total quantity equation $p + 4t + 3t + 2t + t = 250$ $p + 10t = 250 \quad \cdots (1)$ Step 2: Total revenue equation $100p + 50(4t) + 40(3t) + 60(2t) + 60t = 15000$ $100p + 200t + 120t + 120t + 60t = 15000$ $100p + 500t = 15000$ $p + 5t = 150 \quad \cdots (2)$ Step 3: Solve (1) and (2) $(1) - (2): \, 5t = 100 \Rightarrow t = 20$ $p = 150 - 5(20) = 150 - 100 = 50$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

detailed_solution.markdown: b>Given: String P (diameter) = $l$ String K (semicircle) = $\dfrac{\pi l}{2}$ After shortening by x: New length of P = $l - x$ (new diameter) New length of K = $\dfrac{\pi l}{2} - x$ (now forms full circle) Condition: Shortened K forms full circle with shortened P as diameter. Circumference of full circle = $\pi \times \text{diameter} = \pi(l-x)$ Setting up equation: $\dfrac{\pi l}{2} - x = \pi(l - x)$ $\dfrac{\pi l}{2} - x = \pi l - \pi x$ $\pi x - x = \pi l - \dfrac{\pi l}{2}$ $x(\pi - 1) = \dfrac{\pi l}{2}$ $\dfrac{x}{l} = \dfrac{\pi}{2(\pi - 1)}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.
